To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we introduce the general framework for building scale-equivariance convolutional networks with steerable filters; 2) we demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed method; 3) we demonstrate state-of-the- art results on the MNIS T -scale dataset and on the ST L-10 dataset in supervised learning.

we propose a novel architecture for scale equivariant convolutional networks, which is computationally efficient, numerically stable, and outperforms the state-of-the-art on the MNIST and STL-10 scale datasets.

we developed a novel scale-equivariant network with steerable filters, that we demonstrated its computational efficiency and numerical robustness and that we achieved state-of-the-art classification results on MNIST-scale and STL-10 datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
building scale-equivariant networks with a minimal set of trainable parameters and with minimal computational complexity.
the generalization of the theory and practice of convolutional neural networks to the case of scale equivariance.
developing the theory and the practice of scale-equivariant convolution and its applications in deep learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method outperforms the state-of-the-art in the supervised setting, and is comparable in the self-supervised setting.
our method is more efficient than previous approaches, and that it is more accurate than previous methods in supervised learning.
our proposed scale-equivariant steerable networks are more efficient, stable, and accurate in the supervised learning regime, and more stable in the unsupervised learning regime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
scale-equivariant convolution is an effective tool to handle scale changes in various computer vision tasks.
we provide an efficient and numerically stable method for scale equivariance, which can be applied to any convolutional network.
we have shown that scale-equivariant convolution is a powerful and efficient tool for scale-invariant deep learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
scale equivariance can be easily achieved by using scale-convolution.
scale equivariance can be achieved by using simple modifications to existing architectures, which can be applied to a broad range of applications.
scale-equivariant networks can be built with a small overhead in computational complexity.
